args.text: When a process description explicitly states that an actor performs an activity, represent that activity as a BPMN task; do not substitute a start event for the activity or omit an activity that precedes a described outcome.

trace.reason: Check whether existing documented guidance already covers faithfully modeling explicitly stated activities, including activity-versus-event substitutions.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.
Use bpmn:task for atomic work when the execution mode is unspecified. A task contains no internal flow.

result.rule: When the description explicitly states that an actor performs an action that initiates the described process: Model the stated action as an activity in the actor’s scope; do not use a start event representing the resulting occurrence as a substitute for that activity. Represent the process start separately with an appropriate start event.

When the description states that an actor identifies or determines a need before subsequent work begins: Model the identification as a task after a start event; do not represent the stated action only as the start event.

When the description says an optional activity may occur after a case reaches its completion, regardless of which outcome completed the case: Model the optional activity as a subsequent activity reached from the applicable completion paths, rather than as a new process start event.

When the description names an activity or milestone for which a BPMN task is being labeled: Label the task to preserve the action and purpose stated in the description; do not substitute a related but different action or milestone.
